report.reasoning: Store layer: a duplicate idempotencyKey is refused outright, not detected-and-logged. On write, appendPortableGovernanceEvent:704-708 either returns an idempotent-replay receipt naming the already-committed event (identical intent) or throws GES-IDEMPOTENCY-CONFLICT (divergent intent) -- no second record is ever created. On read, scanStream:475-479 throws GES-DUPLICATE/GES-IDEMPOTENCY-CONFLICT, and every replay entry point routes through it, so an out-of-band duplicate makes the whole projection fail rather than return successful. That satisfies R-AC-09's consequent for the STORE's identity. But R-AC-09 governs offer/authority-link/candidate-policy-binding/outcome-evidence replay, and every correlation in that family resolves through the lifecycle eventId (offerEventId, supersedesEventId; agent-decision-journal.mjs:156,166). The envelope keeps eventId and idempotencyKey as two independent free tokens (governance-event.mjs:165-166) with no derivation rule, and no scan indexes eventId. So two records carrying one lifecycle eventId under different idempotency keys both land and both replay as integrity 'valid', leaving a dependent outcome's offerEventId resolving to more than one record. Read in the company of its sibling triggers (missing/stale/substituted/cross-repository/contradictory -- all about an untrustworthy reference), 'duplicated' means the reference resolves to more than one record; reading it as the store's identical-bytes retry case would leave the criterion's own word doing no work at this layer, and identical duplicates are exactly the case the already-enforced 'contradictory' trigger cannot catch.

The absence of any production wiring from recordCommandOffer's append to appendPortableGovernanceEvent -- noted, not built; that is a separate integration scope.
deviations: `journaled` is OPTIONAL, not mandatory. Making it mandatory would have broken every existing caller and the DoD's 'pre-existing cases pass unmodified' requirement. Consequence, stated plainly: when a caller omits `journaled`, duplicate refusal at the recording seam does not fire and remains delegated to the store's idempotencyKey (its own identity only). The replay projector is unconditional.

The second rule (two evidences for one offerEventId) is restricted to an identical `state` and admits an explicit supersedesEventId link. A pair disagreeing in `state` is contradiction, a different trigger word, and is deliberately not reinterpreted as duplication -- forbidding two differing outcomes would have been unbriefed policy invention.
Evidence artifact written via node's --test-reporter-destination rather than a shell redirect; the lifecycle guard rejects redirects (GUARD-PARSE-UNSUPPORTED).
The commit-message file lives in the evidence dir, not the scratchpad: the guard blocks writes outside the physical project root (GUARD-CROSS-REPO-MUTATION). It is left uncommitted.
openItems: dispatch-record.json and commit-msg.txt are intentionally left UNCOMMITTED: the record's report field is written after the commit, so committing it earlier would have persisted a knowingly stale record. The Elephant should land (or discard) both.

Elephant to re-verify independently and decide the R-AC-09 verdict wording in the evidence map; the criterion now has enforcement for the 'duplicated' word at this layer, but the store-layer paragraph in the current pointer text should be corrected -- it credits a mechanism that covers a different identity.

Genuine architecture question for the Elephant, deliberately not acted on: nothing anywhere binds a governance envelope's idempotencyKey to the payload's lifecycle eventId, and no stream scan enforces eventId uniqueness. Any future production wiring of `append` should derive idempotencyKey from eventId, otherwise the store cannot help at all. A defence in governance-event-store.mjs was out of scope by briefing.
